evidence: Standard summer route: a non-technical Class 2 climb over boulder ridges and ash slopes to the crater rim.
Winter route from Marble Mountain Sno-Park: a non-technical snow climb that joins Monitor Ridge below the summit; ice axe and crampons needed.
Easiest route is from First Divide (14 mi up the North Fork Skokomish), following the ridge west; rated class 1.
note: Off-trail ridge walking; lingering snow can make it harder early in the season.

evidence: From Marmot Lake a creek leads into the west-side amphitheater where 'easy slopes lead to the summit'; both routes rated class 1.
note: The record's 'Class 2-3 (steep snow early season)' is not supported; early-season steep snow is a seasonal hazard, not the route's grade.

evidence: Class 2/3 scramble: a gully west of the summit to the ridge, then an exposed ridge traverse; final scramble described as simple Class 2 with exposure, with Class 4/5 gendarmes avoided.
note: Snow-free and wet, the gully is reported as very difficult; no source rates the normal line Class 4.

evidence: MP: 3rd, Easy Snow; St. Peter's Gate needs Class 2-3 scrambling on loose talus and scree; the west-ridge summit finish is a Class 2-3 scramble.
note: A Class 3-4 gully on Stone's south face is an off-route variation, not the traverse.

evidence: MP South Couloir: 4th; 'mostly 2nd and 3rd class with ... one step of 4th class terrain near the summit pinnacle' (Olympic guide says 3rd class).
identity: Describes the same South Couloir line from Lake of the Angels as wa_mount_stone_putvin (same face, approach and crux); likely a duplicate.

evidence: MP South Couloir: 4th; mostly 2nd-3rd class with one 4th-class step on the east side of the summit pinnacle.
identity: Same South Couloir route via the Putvin Trail and Lake of the Angels as wa_mount_stone_lake_of_angels; likely a duplicate.

evidence: MP: 5.10d, 8 pitches, 900 ft; crux 5.10d stemming pitch (Wertkin, Holsten, Westman 2011).
MP lists King Kong - Gorillas Direct Direct at 5.12a; crux is the two-pitch direct headwall finish.
MP: 3rd, Easy Snow; scree couloir then a short exposed Class 3 scramble from the false summit to the true summit.
MP: 5.11-, WI2, Steep Snow; three crack pitches on the pillar are the crux after the steep Ice Cliff Glacier approach.
note: Also WI2 on the glacier approach.

evidence: MP: AI2-3 Steep Snow, Grade III, 2,000 ft (Prater, Prater, Mahre 1957).
note: Late-season rock variations reach low 5th to 5.8; ice is the route's crux.

evidence: MP North Ridge 5.9; 'Complete North Ridge (5.9, 3000 ft)'; the crux is the Great Gendarme's two 5.9 pitches.
note: Starting at the true toe (the 1970 direct start) adds a 5.9+ lieback; MP grades that variant 5.9+.
identity: The breakdown (5.7, 5.8, 5.4, 5.9+ ...) overlaps the separate 'Direct North Ridge w/ Gendarme' row; the two rows may describe the same full-length line.

evidence: MP: WI2-3 M5-; mostly 40-50 degree snow with a narrow 60-80 degree ice step as the crux, then a low-to-mid 5th West Ridge finish.
note: M5- applies when the crux step is thin mixed ground; the record's rock_grade held that mixed grade, not a rock grade.

evidence: The Great Gendarme's two crux pitches (lieback, then offwidth) are graded 5.9 on the North Ridge; some call the offwidth 5.9+.
identity: This is the crux section of the North Ridge, not a separate route to the summit.

evidence: MP: 5.6, Steep Snow; mostly 3rd and 4th class with a couple of low-5th steps and a 5.6 crux.
MP lists 'Always the Cowboy, Never the Cow' at AI5 M5.
note: Also M5 mixed; no route detail beyond the MP listing found.

evidence: MP: 4th, Mod. Snow; other descriptions give Grade II, snow to 40 degrees, then simple Class 3 ridge scrambling to the summit.
note: MP (4th) preferred over the Class 3 elsewhere. Sources call it Grade II, not III.

evidence: MP lists South Headwall at 5.8.
MP Direct North Ridge: 5.9+; the direct start adds ~800 ft and four technical pitches up to 5.9 before the Gendarme.
MP North Ridge (upper, from the notch): 5.9; 11 pitches of low/mid 5th then two 5.9 crux pitches on the Gendarme.
SummitPost: the Southwest Ridge route is Class 2, with optional Class 3 bypasses; trip reports note a few Class 2-3 rock steps on a steep boot track.
note: Some trip reports describe Class 2-3 rock steps; Class 3 if those are counted.

evidence: Long trail via Rachor Pass; 'a short hike and an easy rock scramble' to the rounded summit.
1961 route (Bell, Cooper, Hiser, Swayne) followed the line of least resistance to a faint buttress on the right: III 5.7.
MP lists East Ridge/SE Face at 5.8; the Cascade Alpine Guide gives a 4-pitch 5.6, but trip reports call the first pitch a hard 5.8 (40 ft vertical, offwidth or finger crack).
note: Beckey's 5.6 is the older grade; MP and recent parties give 5.8.

evidence: MP: 5.8, Grade IV, 2,500 ft; thousands of feet of low-fifth to 5.8 on the crest (Stoddard, solo, 1984).
MP: 5.6; a loose gully to the Terror-Rake notch, short low-5th to 5.6 climbing, then 3rd/4th class to the summit.
MP: East Ridge 4th; 'spicy 4th class', often roped on descent.
MP: 5.6, 6 pitches; Grade II with class 4 and low 5th, a single 5.6 move off the first belay.
Easiest route: glacier travel on the White Glacier plus Class 3 scrambling.
note: No source gives a water-ice grade; the record's WI2-3 contradicts a non-technical glacier route.

evidence: MP: 5.4, 4 pitches, ~1,000 ft; slab steps, loose 4th class gully, a short dihedral.
MP: 5.6, Grade IV, steep snow; crux is the 5.6 tower pitch on Forbidden's West Ridge finish.
note: Also a steep snow/ice traverse on the Forbidden Glacier side, conditions-dependent.

evidence: Maintained Mt. Townsend Trail #839 to the summit: 8.2 mi round trip, 2,900 ft gain, no scrambling.
MP: 5.6 PG13; other sources give 5.7 for the short offwidth crux, with mostly 4th and low-5th ridge climbing.
note: Sources split 5.6 (MP) vs 5.7 (Mountaineers, trip reports); MP preferred by rule. Use 5.7 if you weight the offwidth reports.

evidence: Easiest route is the class 4 west route from near Triumph Pass; seldom used and treacherous when wet.
Easiest route: scramble class 3 via the West Side or Gray Wolf Ridge.
Standard south route: Grade I, Class 3, with the 'hourglass' a short pitch of 4th class climbing on the way to the summit.
MP: Winter Direct 4th, AI1-2 Steep Snow, Grade II; climbed only when snow-covered, with two tools and rock and ice protection.
note: The crux pitch is 4th-class chossy rock and steep snow; AI1-2 ice is also listed. MP 'Steep Snow' noted.

evidence: MP: SE Ridge AKA Shield Wall 5.7 R, 13 pitches, Grade III.
